correctness.rationale: For pairs of independent uniform involutions, prescribing ordered disjoint copies of total size M gives a factor (n)_M times each inverse automorphism order, and fixing the two restrictions contributes (I_{n-M}/I_n)^2∼n^{-M}. The resulting mixed factorial moments are precisely those of independent Poissons, including the doubled two-vertex cycle. Translating terms into binary graphs with fixed-point loops preserves the degree bound two. A rooted ball closed under both functions is an actual component, so counts of such roots are integer linear combinations of bounded-size component counts. An open ball can be embedded in paths of arbitrarily large odd sizes by extending beyond an open end; the joint Poisson law for any number of distinct such sizes makes its root count exceed every fixed cutoff with probability tending to one. Effective bounded-degree Hanf locality then reduces each fixed sentence to a finite Boolean function of truncated small-component counts. A finite representative can add long odd paths without changing any closed-ball counts. Poisson tails at positive rational means are rational polynomials in their exponentials, giving the common-denominator ring exactly as claimed. For arbitrarily many distinct odd sizes the presence indicators have independent Bernoulli limits with parameter 1-e^{-1}; arbitrary unions of atoms approximate any target within the largest atom weight, which decays to zero. An independent bounded enumeration through n=4 enumerated all involutions as partitions into singletons and transpositions, paired them, evaluated six selected component factorial moments at each size, and agreed with the exact formula; e.g. six of 16 pairs have the three-vertex path at n=3. This is not a proof of locality or the limit. The frozen verification material was inspected, not executed.
